newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan coffee board says auctions resume July 22.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan coffee board says auctions resume July 22.

text.p: The Coffee Board of Kenya (CBK) said on Friday that coffee export auctions would resume on July 22 after a two-week suspension caused by acute shortages.
In a statement read to Reuters, CBK official Charles Gatere said " ... due to inadequate supply of coffee, auctions will close for the next two weeks. Auctions will resume on July 22."
Gatere denied reports from officials at the Kenya Coffee Auctions Limited who said the suspension was indefinite.
"There has been a misunderstanding. Auctions will certainly resume on the July 22 and will continue normally (every week) from then on," he added.

Drought that ravaged most growing areas of East Africa from October last year and persisted to March had forced a severe cut in coffee production and coffee reaching the market from farmers was well below earlier predictions, CBK field monitors said.
